title: Federal reserve data on fab utilization
gist: A shared X post citing Federal Reserve data shows US chip plants at record output but running at 2017-era utilization (~72.2%, down from 92.2%), as capacity outpaced output; commenter Ashwin Rao frames it as a risk that downstream demand has hit an implementation capacity wall.

insights.claim: US chip plants printed their biggest month of output on record while running at 2017-era utilization rates, according to a shared X post citing Federal Reserve data.
insights.speaker: @nodiligence
insights.so_what: Capacity is being added faster than it is being used, a potential margin and returns risk.
insights.quote: us chip plants just printed their biggest month of output on record and they're running at 2017 utilisation rates.

insights.claim: The Fed's capacity index for semiconductors and electronic components is up 80% since February 2022 while output is up 41%, so utilization fell from 92.2% to 72.2%.
insights.speaker: @nodiligence
insights.so_what: Widening gap between capacity and output pressures fab economic returns.
insights.quote: the fed's capacity index for semiconductors and electronic components is up 80% since february 2022 and output is up 41%, so utilisation went 92.2% to 72.2%.

insights.claim: Production rates need to rise faster for fabs to generate economic returns, but downstream chip consumers have hit an implementation capacity wall from regulatory approvals, labor availability and utility availability.
insights.speaker: Ashwin Rao
insights.so_what: Demand-absorption bottlenecks downstream could cap fab utilization and returns despite capacity growth.

insights.claim: The commenter notes the utilization data's compilation method and validity are uncertain but finds it interesting from a risk perspective.
insights.speaker: Ashwin Rao
insights.so_what: Flags that the figures are unverified and should be treated cautiously.
